title: U.S. House · Utah's 2nd District
area: Northern Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 1st District, including Ogden and parts of Davis and Weber counties.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. As a result, incumbent Blake Moore — who represented the old 1st District — is running for this newly drawn 2nd District rather than a district with the same boundaries he previously held. Moore defeated Karianne Lisonbee 57.8%-42.2% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Blake Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Karianne Lisonbee 57.8%-42.2% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Utah's 1st District (since 2021); Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference

summary.text: Blake Moore is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election, running in the newly drawn 2nd District after previously representing the old 1st District since 2021. He is Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference and sits on the Ways and Means Committee, and is running on tax cuts, economic growth and support for Hill Air Force Base.

background.text: Born in Ogden, Utah in 1980; earned a B.A. in behavioral science and health from the University of Utah and an M.A. in public policy and administration from Northwestern University.

Worked as an international healthcare consultant with DocBerry International, a foreign service officer with the U.S. Department of State, and an executive with the Cicero Group before entering Congress.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2020 and re-elected since; currently sits on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health, Social Security and Trade subcommittees) and the House Committee on Budget.

priorities.text: Says he helped draft tax-cut legislation that doubled the child tax credit, ended taxes on tips, car-loan interest, Social Security benefits and overtime, and increased wages "by up to $7,200 per worker."
As co-chair of the House Air Force Caucus and House Depot Caucus, says he has worked to secure funding and infrastructure for Hill Air Force Base and Utah's defense workforce.
Says he prioritizes secure borders and a "lawful immigration system," and supports House Republican border security legislation.

positions.summary: Says he helped draft and pass tax cuts and opposes raising taxes, framing his work as preventing what he calls "the largest tax hike in history."
Supports House Republican border security legislation and describes his approach as protecting public safety and upholding "the rule of law."

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health, Social Security, and Trade subcommittees) and the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Peter Crosby
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled; also withdrew from the 1st District Democratic primary earlier in 2026

summary.text: Peter Crosby is the Democratic nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. He works in corporate analytics and as an adjunct professor.

background.text: Career experience includes working in corporate analytics and as an adjunct professor.

candidates.name: Carlton Bowen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 10, 2026 Independent American Party of Utah convention

summary.text: Carlton Bowen is the Independent American Party of Utah nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. He is a U.S. Air Force veteran and current member of the American Fork City Council who works as an IT project manager.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1988 to 1994; earned an associate degree in imagery and intelligence analysis from the Community College of the Air Force and a bachelor's degree in economics from Weber State University.
Works as a senior IT project manager at Intermountain Healthcare.
Currently serves on the American Fork, Utah city council.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey found beyond basic biographical facts and his local council role.

candidates.name: Daniel Cottam
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention

summary.text: Daniel Cottam is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. He is a bariatric surgeon and business owner.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University and a medical degree from the University of Texas Health Science Center, San Antonio (1997).
Career experience includes working as a business owner, bariatric surgeon, and consultant with Medtronic.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey found beyond basic biographical facts.

summary.text: Robert Moesinger is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 2nd Congressional District. He is a systems/automation engineer running primarily on breaking up the two-party system rather than a traditional left-right platform.

background.text: Graduated from Ogden High School and earned a degree from the University of Utah (2018).

priorities.text: Argues the core problem in American politics is the two-party system itself, which he says creates bad incentives for representatives; supports moving toward a multi-party system to increase voter choice and legislative independence.
priorities.quote: An election that sends a Republican or Democrat to their respective Washington trench fortifies the dominance and dysfunction of the two parties.
